title: Boundary reduction kills the zeroth component
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a first-quadrant homological double complex of $R$-modules with commuting horizontal and vertical differentials $d$ and $\delta$. Write $T_n(A)$, $Z_n(A)$ and $D_{n+1}:T_{n+1}(A)\to T_n(A)$ for its zig-zag total module, cycle submodule and boundary map [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. Assume each row is exact at every positive horizontal index [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Let $C_q=\operatorname{coker}(d:A_{1,q}\to A_{0,q})$, with projection $\pi_q$ and differential induced by $\delta$, a chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. If $n\ge0$, $a\in Z_n(A)$, and there is $y\in C_{n+1}$ with $\delta_C y=\pi_n(a_{0,n})$, then there is $b\in T_{n+1}(A)$ such that $a-D_{n+1}b\in Z_n(A)$ and $(a-D_{n+1}b)_{0,n}=0$.

proof.text: Use the first clause of exists_zigzagToRowCokernel to obtain surjectivity and kernel-image equality for every row-cokernel projection. Lift the boundary witness y to c in A_(0,n+1). The chain-map identity implies that a_(0,n)-delta(c) is killed by pi_n. The same clause supplies e in A_(1,n) with d(e)=a_(0,n)-delta(c).

Take b to be the direct-sum tuple supported at (0,n+1) and (1,n) with entries c and e. By definition the zeroth component of its boundary is delta(c)+d(e)=a_(0,n). Boundaries lie in cycles by the first clause of the functoriality theorem; subtracting gives the required residual cycle.

theorem zigzag_boundary_reduction
    (A : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ)
      (ComplexShape.down ℕ))
    (hrow : ∀ (p q : ℕ), 0 < p →
      (ShortComplex.mk ((A.d (p + 1) p).f q) ((A.d p (p - 1)).f q)
        (by rw [← HomologicalComplex.comp_f, A.d_comp_d,
          HomologicalComplex.zero_f])).Exact)
    (n : ℕ) (a : zigzagTotal A n) (ha : a ∈ zigzagCycles A n)
    (hboundary : ∃ y : (A.opcycles 0).X (n + 1),
      (A.opcycles 0).d (n + 1) n y = (A.pOpcycles 0).f n
        (DirectSum.component R (ZigzagIndex n)
          (fun i : ZigzagIndex n => (A.X i.1.1).X i.1.2) ⟨(0, n), by simp⟩ a)) :
    ∃ b : zigzagTotal A (n + 1),
      a - zigzagBoundary A n b ∈ zigzagCycles A n ∧
      DirectSum.component R (ZigzagIndex n)
        (fun i : ZigzagIndex n => (A.X i.1.1).X i.1.2)
        ⟨(0, n), by simp⟩ (a - zigzagBoundary A n b) = 0
